normalization.title: Uncensored, Private, or Sovereign?
normalization.overview: Jack Roberts presents five levels of control over AI, from less restrictive hosted models and a second-model checker to always-available hosting, images and video, and local inference. The Reader distinguishes his demonstrations from the separate questions of privacy, reliability and operational sovereignty.
normalization.whyItMatters: Operators considering an uncensored service, self-hosted model or mobile deployment need to distinguish refusal policy, data custody and control of the complete system. The video is a useful survey of options, not proof that a model is accurate, private or independent of its surrounding services.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Control is a system property, not a model label. Audit weights, inference location, service dependencies, access boundaries, durable context and revocation separately, then validate claimed behavior under tests that include error handling and pressure to agree.

archiveCall.label: Test the whole boundary
archiveCall.text: Evaluate the model, hosting, memory, network control and verification path together before claiming independence.

normalization.falsification: Repeat the bounded model tests, inspect data flows and third-party dependencies, and check whether observed behavior survives matched prompts, adversarial claims and a loss of external service access.
normalization.freshness: November 2026 video and bounded local/hosted experiments; not a representative model benchmark.
